steps.text: Part 2 of 4: The bishop in a busy position. This part covers Try it. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

steps.caption: At the start the bishop on c1 has no move at all. Its neighbours on b2 and d2 are White's own pawns.

line.say: A pawn steps out of the way and opens the bishop's diagonal.
Black answers in the centre with a pawn of his own.
Now the bishop slides out to f4, which was impossible a moment ago.

steps.caption: After 1.d4 d5 the bishop on c1 can reach five squares.

line.say: It slides to the far end of this diagonal, h6.

steps.caption: After the e-pawn moves, the other bishop wakes up as well: five squares for the bishop on f1.

line.say: The bishop swings out along its diagonal toward the black side.
Black develops a knight, a piece we have not yet used.

steps.text: Pawns often start in the bishop's way, so a pawn move can wake a bishop up. Capablanca's advice, as summarised in our notes (*Chess Fundamentals*, paraphrased), is to start with a centre pawn partly because it frees a bishop and the queen. You have just watched it happen twice. [H] A habit worth trying: before moving a bishop, look at what is shutting it in.

steps.caption: Two of its own pawns shut the bishop in completely. No moves.

line.say: Moving one pawn opens a line again.
Black makes a waiting move with the king.
Now the bishop can step out along the diagonal the pawn left.

steps.caption: A busy middlegame position. The bishop on c1 has a line out through d2, because the d-pawn has gone to d3.

line.say: It goes to the edge of its diagonal; nothing of either side stands in the way.
[I] h6 asks the bishop where it will go; it can retreat or take on f6.

steps.title: One change at a time
steps.prompt: Predict the squares in each position before opening the next one. The first is the reference; then one black pawn is added; then a rook moves.

steps.text: Your routine before any bishop move. Say the piece's name. Look along each of its four diagonals. Stop at the first piece in the way: if it is yours, stop one square short; if it is the enemy's, you may land on it. Last, check that the square you want is on your list. Do this out loud for a while; it will become automatic.
